Entire-Checkpoint: 58a791aa54c1","messageHeadline":"refactor: fold the overview into the row it is context for","oid":"62c3aa4dcc157fda34eb0faf2c16d963af137bc8"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T12:50:16Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T12:50:16Z","messageBody":"Two things made the figure look accidental: the cells grew to fill the
rail, and the window was a variable number of months, so the same habit
drew a different shape every visit. It is now the reference's geometry
exactly — 12px blocks, 2px gutters, a 22px label band — over 53 columns
that are 53 columns on every day of the week.

The '10B tokens' subline is gone. In its place are four nested windows on
the same number, all but the first summed from the very series the cells
are drawn from, so the figures cannot drift out of agreement with the
picture under them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 5bfc8fc4be09","messageHeadline":"feat: draw the activity plate at a fixed size on a rolling year","oid":"81f332e9bed6a10049291cd637ccb5249063d07f"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T12:52:57Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T12:52:57Z","messageBody":"Tags without pills was the worst of both: four words joined by dots that
looked like a caption and read like a list. The two that are labels — the
language and the third-party fact — are pills now; the year has moved up
beside the title, where it can be read without opening the row, and the
host stays in the link, which is the only place it means anything.

Three of the eight projects ship a mark of their own. Those are checked
in rather than fetched, so a row never depends on another origin being
up. The silhouettes are drawn as masks in the row's own ink so the gutter
stays one colour; the one mark that carries its own is drawn grey and
colours under the pointer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 77da115eb7cf","messageHeadline":"feat: give project rows their own marks and real tag pills","oid":"3d6e54e501736ed32876e570b1580cbc3a87e535"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T12:54:24Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T12:54:24Z","messageBody":"The reference draws posts as a two-column grid because every one of its
posts ships a cover; a grid of pictures is what a grid is for. Ours ship
none, so each card was a row that had been put in a box — half the width,
summary breaking after four words, and at one post a card beside a hole.

The cover is optional now and the row is not: when one exists it leads
the row as a 16:9 plate, when it does not the row is a title, a sentence
and two facts. Same shape as a project row, which is the site's idiom,
and it reads the same at one post as at fifty.

The 'notes on coding agents' subline is gone with it — the panel title
and five titles under it already say what the blog is about.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 3dd3c880b9ce","messageHeadline":"feat: lay posts out as rows rather than as cards with no pictures","oid":"775c55f833efdacccf2dbb9bdf0caa225b01fd44"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T17:30:21Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T17:30:21Z","messageBody":"The footer said 'Dhruv Sharma' one line above a wordmark reading
dhruv2mars; the two now agree. The mailbox has left the row — the
overview's 'say hi' is the directory and answers 'how do I reach this
person', while the footer is a signature and carries the three places the
work lives plus the feed, which belongs to the site rather than to the
person. The hairline rules between the glyphs are gone with it, along
with the one that used to trail the last of them.

The feed gained the three declarations readers actually use: an
atom:link rel=self so a reader handed the file by any route knows where
to poll, a lastBuildDate so it can ask what changed without downloading
everything, and a language. The auto-discovery link now carries a title,
which is what a reader files the subscription under — and it is how most
people subscribe, by handing over dhruv2mars.com and never seeing
/feed.xml at all.

Entire-Checkpoint: 7d759ac4e0d5","messageHeadline":"feat: sign the footer with the mark, and make the feed a real feed","oid":"7f4e812454cb55575cf72d79631facb5dc18e3b0"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T17:39:51Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T17:39:51Z","messageBody":"The wordmark played a one-shot wipe on scroll and then sat inert. The
reference's logotype is alive: an outline that is always there, filled
through a gradient whose near end is tied to the cursor, so the ink runs
away from the pointer and washes from one side of the name to the other.

Same construction here, over our own cell set: a hairline pass and a
gradient pass over one <defs> group, x1 sprung at the reference's
150/25, resting at the horizontal middle. At rest that makes the
gradient vertical — the letters ink from the baseline up and fade to
outline at the top — so a phone, which never sends a pointer, still gets
a finished drawing rather than an empty one.

Entire-Checkpoint: 18a698a64c76","messageHeadline":"feat: let the footer signature take its ink from the pointer","oid":"bc9be6620785cd031ada6918d2c79b260feedd78"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T17:44:34Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T17:44:34Z","messageBody":"The index was the home page's section with a bigger heading. It is a
page: it gets the panel, the count, and a search field over the whole
list, which is the thing the reference has that we did not.

The query stays in component state rather than the URL — the reference
pays a query-state dependency, a Suspense boundary and a router write
per keystroke for a shareable filtered index, and nobody shares one.

Rows are drawn client-side now so they can be filtered, so the Post
shape, the date formatter and the matcher move to lib/posts, which has
no filesystem in it; lib/blog keeps the disk. Bodies are dropped before
the list crosses to the browser.

The footer needed no decision: it is in the root layout, so it already
closes every route, which is the standard practice it was measured
against.

Entire-Checkpoint: ce1c27db08b0","messageHeadline":"feat: give the blog index a filter and one frame","oid":"904a96671fedff008694606421f4d7a776ac84e4"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T22:44:02Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T22:44:02Z","messageBody":"The post page was a title and a body. It is now a document you can do
something with: copy it as Markdown, hand it to a model, share it, and
step to the post either side without going back to the index first.

- `lib/slug.ts` holds the one `slugify`, so the renderer's heading ids
  and the contents list cannot drift apart.
- `lib/toc.ts` reads the headings out of the MDX source, skipping fenced
  blocks so a `#` in a shell snippet is not a section.
- `findNeighbours` and `postMarkdown` join `lib/posts.ts`; the markdown
  builder is shared with the new `/blog/<slug>/raw.md` route, which is
  what the "Open in ChatGPT / Claude" items point a model at.
- `components/menu.tsx` is the site's first dropdown: the ARIA menu
  button contract, arrows, Home/End, Escape, outside click, ~130 lines,
  no dependency.
- The arrows are labelled "Newer" and "Older" rather than
  "Previous"/"Next" — in a reverse-chronological list those words are a
  coin toss, and the label is the only thing saying which way time runs.
- The reference's sticky minimap is deliberately not ported: this frame
  is one railed column with no margin to float anything in, so the
  contents sit at the front where a contents page has always sat.

- `searchProjects` reads the language, kind, note and year as well as

- `components/search-field.tsx` is the field itself, shared, so the

- `ProjectsSection` loses its `as` prop and goes back to being what it

Entire-Checkpoint: adb382e6def5","messageHeadline":"fix: stop the contents list from reading as a wall of rules","oid":"87959d5e24f07de81d0b151f4c427e5ff1d2ee74"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T23:07:02Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T23:07:02Z","messageBody":"The wordmark's outline was drawn in `--line`, which is the hairline

hairline; simply a visible one, in both themes.

plate and the white screen fill are dropped so the alpha is the line
work, and the row draws it in its own ink like relunar and gunmetal.

pi-queue, mdv-ts, and codexchat ship no mark and keep their kind glyph.

The rotating subline entered from above and left below, so the sentence read
as falling. Both halves now travel up: the arriving line rises from below the
baseline and the leaving one continues out the top. The exit also drops its
own separate easing curve, so enter and exit are one gesture.

Project rows go back to a name and two doors — the row opens the record in
place, the arrow leaves for the thing itself. The repository icon goes; a row
that carried three controls made the reader pick one before knowing what the
project was. Marks, logos and tag pills are unchanged, they just live in the
record instead of the row.

Entire-Checkpoint: d4d44c48daaa","messageHeadline":"fix: send the role line upwards and give project rows their disclosur…","oid":"9b599be2a7e75dec47a7f1a70d029e6c2707af92"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-21T08:13:18Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T08:13:18Z","messageBody":"A browser voice reading /dʱruːʋ ˈʃərmə/ off an English phoneme set has
neither the breathy-voiced d nor the retroflex v, so it says a different
name confidently — worse than saying nothing. Ship a recording instead
and drop the respelling that only existed to feed the synthesiser.

Playback goes through Web Audio rather than an <audio> element: the clip
is decoded once per document, so a second press replays from memory on
the same frame. The context is built on the press, so a visitor who never
clicks never opens one.

Redraw VolumeIcon on the reference's own geometry — stroked cone rather
than filled, waves stepped down from its 24px grid onto ours.

Entire-Checkpoint: c2f8c1d306ea","messageHeadline":"feat: rebuild the blog and 404 routes on the frame system","oid":"4c0f7d2e02e459b141a53e249a7f565182720cdb"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-17T23:39:02Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-17T23:39:24Z","messageBody":"Four defects the audit caught, each re-measured in a real browser before
and after the change:

- The mobile header clipped its own theme toggle. Below `sm` the bar now
  collapses to the mark plus compact controls, and the palette trigger
  goes with the nav — a touch viewport has no Cmd-K. The last control now
  ends 17px inside a 390px viewport instead of 1px outside it.
- The activity mosaic overflowed its rail on a phone. Narrowed to 26
  columns and given inline padding for the focus ring, so the grid's
  scrollWidth equals its container's at 390px.
- The hero figure was a solid cube floating in an empty plate. Rebuilt as
  hatched line-art on a floor lattice that runs off all four edges to be
  cut there, and scaled to cover the plate rather than sit inside it.
- Two diagonal bands met back-to-back above the footer. Bands go between
  panels; the footer opens with its own.

And the six polish items from the same pass:

- Footer rebuilt as ruled two-column rows with real colophon entries and
  a rule between every social glyph, not only before the last.
- Project rows carry a glyph for what the project is — terminal, queue,
  device, server, document, canvas, chat, VM — instead of repeating the
  brand cube eight times.
- Hero density matched to the reference: a 128/160px portrait slot and a
  plate the drawing fills.
- Nav labels are title-case; the palette no longer has to re-case them.
- One focus ring for the whole site, drawn on the mosaic's active
  descendant rather than around all 365 cells.
- A margin note on the mosaic, in the hand it would be written in, shown
  only where there is both a cursor to aim and a gutter to hold it.

Hero and footer geometry verified against the reference at 390px and
1440px: hero 374x372 vs 374x377 on a phone, 768x461 vs 768x463 on
desktop, portrait slot identical at both.

Entire-Checkpoint: 3cdf38d3c9c4","messageHeadline":"fix: close the round-two gaps found against the reference","oid":"ecb06aa795c8e057c26e69273971ff6982d8beca"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-18T00:11:12Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-18T00:11:12Z","messageBody":"The round-three audit drove both sites in a real browser and scored 77/100,
confirming eight of the ten round-two claims and finding three new defects.
This closes all of them.

Duplicate stripe bands on every non-home route. The round-two fix that
removed the trailing band was applied to the home page only, so /blog, a
blog post, and the 404 shell each still emitted one directly above the
footer's own — a double border on every route but one. All three now end on
the panel's own hairline, matching the home page.

The 404 left the frame hanging in a void. Its rail stopped under a short
panel and resumed at the footer with unused viewport between. `main` is now
a flex column so a short route can grow a railed spacer down to the footer;
the 404 fills the viewport exactly rather than stretching around a gap.

/blog advertised itself as "Blog" while returning 404. With nothing
published the route calls `notFound()`, but its static metadata still
titled the tab, naming a page the Visitor cannot reach. Metadata is now
derived from whether any Post exists, and both 404 surfaces read the same.

The hero no longer ships a visible placeholder. "portrait pending" made the
primary identity block read as unfinished at every size; the monogram plate
now stands as a deliberate mark and the rationale moved onto `Avatar`.

The footer is a ruled matrix rather than a gapped stack. Every row is a cell
with a hairline beneath it and a rule between label and value, so the
colophon reads in the same frame grammar as the panels above it.

Also: the floor lattice is carried past the content rail as a whisper, so
the hero drawing reads as larger than the frame that crops it — a detail the
reference has and we did not; the command palette's active row now carries
the same focus ring the activity grid draws on its active cell, so "where am
I" looks the same in both widgets; and row hover was raised in both themes,
where `--accent-muted` at 20% of accent in dark was barely legible.

Entire-Checkpoint: 158211e5d399","messageHeadline":"fix: adopt the reference details the round-seven audit confirmed","oid":"3b5c9490fc00bf81fe8dce97eb13fcdf8f7cdede"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-18T09:41:14Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-18T09:41:14Z","messageBody":"Eight findings were raised against the reference; five were real.

- The activity strip no longer drops half the year on a phone. All 53

  with scroll-driven edge fades that appear only while there is more
  grid past them — the reference's own answer, and the only one that
  keeps the caption's "last 12 months" honest.
- The command palette holds a fixed 48/320/40 shape, so a query that
  matches nothing no longer collapses the dialog. The new legend row
  names what Enter will do to the highlighted row rather than promising

- Icon controls carry the reference's 8px corner, not 6px, and their

wrapper is `h-12.5 border-t border-line py-1 pl-4 sm:h-9`, class for

site's own, and it already yields to reduced-motion.

Entire-Checkpoint: 958e2865b8ae","messageHeadline":"fix: let the activity caption wrap the way the reference's does","oid":"10755c3ccf3936bf8192aaa7cb8d6d6e20a2b34a"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-18T10:03:49Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-18T10:03:49Z","messageBody":"A panel title is an h2 because a panel is normally one section of a page
that already has its own h1. But three pages *are* one panel — a post,
the blog index, the 404 — and those were shipping with no h1 at all, and
with the post's title ranked level with its own section headings.

The reference does the obvious thing: h1 for the post title, h1 for the
blog index, h1 for the 404. So PanelTitle takes `as`, and those three
pass "h1".

The post title also carried a `text-2xl` that never applied — cn() joins
classes rather than merging them, so the base text-3xl won on stylesheet
order. Dropped rather than forced: the reference's post title is the
largest thing on its page, and at text-3xl ours now is too.

Entire-Checkpoint: fc496cd20058","messageHeadline":"fix: close the round-nine gaps found against the reference","oid":"06106dd35a31b51f49c1d7b565a9954a5e048687"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-18T10:21:29Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-18T10:21:29Z","messageBody":"Three differences, each measured on the live reference before and after:

- The hatched bands were in the wrong places. The reference bands the
  hero off from the panels and then runs overview, links and the
  contribution grid as one uninterrupted block; ours ran the hero
  straight into Overview and then cut the block in half before the
  activity grid. Bands group panels, they do not separate every one.
  Reference: hero ends 519, band 519-551, Overview 551, Social 744,
  Contributions 808, band 995. Ours now: hero 517, band 517-549,
  Overview 549, Social 629, Activity 693, band 1001.
- The social buttons were a translucent tint on the hairline colour with
  muted glyphs. The reference draws them on the page background with the
  border token and foreground/80, and switches to a white wash in dark.
  Ours now computes byte-identical in both themes, at rest and on hover.
- Every hover that landed on accent-foreground now lands on foreground,
  which is where the reference's own hovers land — measured on its theme
  toggle, its social buttons and its header buttons alike.

Not taken, with the measurement that rules each out:

- "Match the reference's focus ring (auto 1px)." That is the browser's
  default, not a designed ring — the reference simply never styles
  :focus-visible. Ours is 2px at 2px offset on every tab stop by
  intent. Adopting the default would make focus harder to see.
- "The activity fade should scale with overflow." It already does. At
  390 the rail hides 406px and the fade is the full 40px; at 1440 it
  hides 12px and the fade is 12px. The reference shows ~0.3px there

Entire-Checkpoint: bd1d78f52f43","messageHeadline":"fix: give the phone a nav and every control a press state","oid":"e0d1f59cbd25e8fbd1d26324bc037b4686115a08"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-18T16:08:08Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-18T16:08:08Z","messageBody":"Measured against the reference, four things were simply absent.

The site had no icons at all — no favicon, no apple-touch icon, no
manifest — so every tab showed a blank page glyph. The mark now draws
itself at favicon scale from the same isometric geometry the header uses,
switching foreground on `prefers-color-scheme` rather than shipping a
second asset.

The viewport meta lacked `viewport-fit=cover`, which meant the dock's
`env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` padding resolved to zero on every notched
phone — the safe-area handling added last commit was dead code.

The share card used a blue square where the mark should be and a set of
greys belonging to no palette on the site, set in whatever sans the
rasteriser happened to have. It is now the real mark, the site's own zinc
ramp, and Geist.

And the nav never marked where you were. The reference marks it in both
places it draws the nav — `text-foreground` in the header, `bg-accent` in
the sheet — and ours marked it in neither, in appearance or in
`aria-current`. Most of our nav points at sections of one long page rather
than at routes, so the answer comes from the scroll, read as the external
store it is. The header's labels also pick up the reference's
`tracking-wide`: measured 0.35px there against `normal` here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: c2ce0b4a3793","messageHeadline":"fix: give the site a face and the nav a sense of place","oid":"1ef322a9ec970b523d3220694299c9f188990203"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T07:04:27Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-19T07:04:27Z","messageBody":"Three things the reference does that we were only half doing.

The dialogs opened but did not close: React unmounts a node the instant
its state says so, so an exit animation never gets a frame to play. A
small presence hook holds each node for the length of its exit and marks
it inert while it leaves, so what is on screen for that tenth of a
second is a picture of a sheet rather than a sheet you can still tab
into. The exits are written as their own keyframes rather than as the
entrance played `reverse` — reversing an animation that has already
finished re-reads the same finished playhead against the other end of
the timeline, which snaps to the far keyframe instead of travelling to
it. The palette backdrop was also outliving the panel it dimmed for;
they now leave together.

The browser's own chrome — the address bar, the task switcher — was
keyed off the reader's OS rather than the theme they picked on the site,
because a media-conditioned `theme-color` pair cannot know about a
manual override. A client tag with no media wins by tree order, so it is
prepended rather than appended.

And the hero plate was a fixed height guessing at its own artwork's
shape. It now carries the ratio the drawing actually has, which measures
569x362.27 at 1440 — the same numbers as the reference.

Entire-Checkpoint: f245a63652e3","messageHeadline":"fix: let the overlays leave, and the browser chrome follow the reader","oid":"3deb19770613ca1099d7e35bf964fac41fa1d2b6"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T07:04:48Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-19T07:04:48Z","messageBody":"Two facts the usual social row cannot carry: a place and an hour.

They sit under the positioning line in the overview, each behind its own
glyph in the reference's icon-tile recipe, in mono, two to a row above
the small breakpoint. The location links to a map search on the same
string it displays, so there is nothing to keep in sync; it is unset for
now and an unset location draws no row rather than an empty pin.

The clock is real. One module-scope store ticks for the whole page and
only while something is subscribed, and the hands on the dial are drawn
from the actual time rather than frozen at ten past ten. The server
renders no time at all — this page is prerendered and revalidates
hourly, so a baked-in hour could be an hour wrong, and a clock that is
briefly blank beats a clock that is briefly wrong. Dashes hold the width
until the real time lands.

The distance to the reader keeps its minutes where the reference floors
to whole hours: from a half-hour zone that floor reports five where the
answer is five and a half, which is wrong rather than round.

The window is chosen rather than fixed — it walks back while the months were
worked in and stops at the first one that was not, so the plate reads as a
habit instead of as the blank half-year before one. Intensity cuts at the
quartiles of the days with work in them, because one 400M-token afternoon
against a hundred ordinary days draws as a single black square otherwise.

The readout moved into the caption: the day under the cursor, in the
magnitude a number this size is read in. Held arrow keys walk on our own
clock, the hover cursor lands without a transition chasing it, and the
LaunchAgent gets /opt/homebrew/bin on PATH — without it tokscale could not
find node and the feed had been silent since July.

Entire-Checkpoint: 77da115eb7cf","messageHeadline":"feat: give project rows their own marks and real tag pills","oid":"3d6e54e501736ed32876e570b1580cbc3a87e535"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T12:54:24Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T12:54:24Z","messageBody":"The reference draws posts as a two-column grid because every one of its
posts ships a cover; a grid of pictures is what a grid is for. Ours ship
none, so each card was a row that had been put in a box — half the width,
summary breaking after four words, and at one post a card beside a hole.

The cover is optional now and the row is not: when one exists it leads
the row as a 16:9 plate, when it does not the row is a title, a sentence
and two facts. Same shape as a project row, which is the site's idiom,
and it reads the same at one post as at fifty.

The 'notes on coding agents' subline is gone with it — the panel title
and five titles under it already say what the blog is about.

Entire-Checkpoint: 3dd3c880b9ce","messageHeadline":"feat: lay posts out as rows rather than as cards with no pictures","oid":"775c55f833efdacccf2dbb9bdf0caa225b01fd44"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T17:30:21Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T17:30:21Z","messageBody":"The footer said 'Dhruv Sharma' one line above a wordmark reading
dhruv2mars; the two now agree. The mailbox has left the row — the
overview's 'say hi' is the directory and answers 'how do I reach this
person', while the footer is a signature and carries the three places the
work lives plus the feed, which belongs to the site rather than to the
person. The hairline rules between the glyphs are gone with it, along
with the one that used to trail the last of them.

The feed gained the three declarations readers actually use: an
atom:link rel=self so a reader handed the file by any route knows where
to poll, a lastBuildDate so it can ask what changed without downloading
everything, and a language. The auto-discovery link now carries a title,
which is what a reader files the subscription under — and it is how most
people subscribe, by handing over dhruv2mars.com and never seeing
/feed.xml at all.

Entire-Checkpoint: 7d759ac4e0d5","messageHeadline":"feat: sign the footer with the mark, and make the feed a real feed","oid":"7f4e812454cb55575cf72d79631facb5dc18e3b0"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T17:39:51Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T17:39:51Z","messageBody":"The wordmark played a one-shot wipe on scroll and then sat inert. The
reference's logotype is alive: an outline that is always there, filled
through a gradient whose near end is tied to the cursor, so the ink runs
away from the pointer and washes from one side of the name to the other.

Same construction here, over our own cell set: a hairline pass and a
gradient pass over one <defs> group, x1 sprung at the reference's
150/25, resting at the horizontal middle. At rest that makes the
gradient vertical — the letters ink from the baseline up and fade to
outline at the top — so a phone, which never sends a pointer, still gets
a finished drawing rather than an empty one.

Entire-Checkpoint: 18a698a64c76","messageHeadline":"feat: let the footer signature take its ink from the pointer","oid":"bc9be6620785cd031ada6918d2c79b260feedd78"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-20T17:44:34Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-20T17:44:34Z","messageBody":"The index was the home page's section with a bigger heading. It is a
page: it gets the panel, the count, and a search field over the whole
list, which is the thing the reference has that we did not.

The query stays in component state rather than the URL — the reference
pays a query-state dependency, a Suspense boundary and a router write
per keystroke for a shareable filtered index, and nobody shares one.

Rows are drawn client-side now so they can be filtered, so the Post
shape, the date formatter and the matcher move to lib/posts, which has
no filesystem in it; lib/blog keeps the disk. Bodies are dropped before
the list crosses to the browser.

The footer needed no decision: it is in the root layout, so it already
closes every route, which is the standard practice it was measured
against.

step to the post either side without going back to the index first.

- `lib/slug.ts` holds the one `slugify`, so the renderer's heading ids
  and the contents list cannot drift apart.
- `lib/toc.ts` reads the headings out of the MDX source, skipping fenced
  blocks so a `#` in a shell snippet is not a section.
- `findNeighbours` and `postMarkdown` join `lib/posts.ts`; the markdown
  builder is shared with the new `/blog/<slug>/raw.md` route, which is

  button contract, arrows, Home/End, Escape, outside click, ~130 lines,

- The arrows are labelled "Newer" and "Older" rather than
  "Previous"/"Next" — in a reverse-chronological list those words are a
  coin toss, and the label is the only thing saying which way time runs.

  is one railed column with no margin to float anything in, so the
  contents sit at the front where a contents page has always sat.

The rotating subline entered from above and left below, so the sentence read
as falling. Both halves now travel up: the arriving line rises from below the
baseline and the leaving one continues out the top. The exit also drops its

Entire-Checkpoint: d4d44c48daaa","messageHeadline":"fix: send the role line upwards and give project rows their disclosur…","oid":"9b599be2a7e75dec47a7f1a70d029e6c2707af92"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-21T08:13:18Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T08:13:18Z","messageBody":"A browser voice reading /dʱruːʋ ˈʃərmə/ off an English phoneme set has

name confidently — worse than saying nothing. Ship a recording instead
and drop the respelling that only existed to feed the synthesiser.

Playback goes through Web Audio rather than an <audio> element: the clip
is decoded once per document, so a second press replays from memory on
the same frame. The context is built on the press, so a visitor who never
clicks never opens one.

Redraw VolumeIcon on the reference's own geometry — stroked cone rather
than filled, waves stepped down from its 24px grid onto ours.

manifest — so every tab showed a blank page glyph. The mark now draws
itself at favicon scale from the same isometric geometry the header uses,

greys belonging to no palette on the site, set in whatever sans the
rasteriser happened to have. It is now the real mark, the site's own zinc

places it draws the nav — `text-foreground` in the header, `bg-accent` in

`tracking-wide`: measured 0.35px there against `normal` here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: c2ce0b4a3793","messageHeadline":"fix: give the site a face and the nav a sense of place","oid":"1ef322a9ec970b523d3220694299c9f188990203"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T07:04:27Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-19T07:04:27Z","messageBody":"Three things the reference does that we were only half doing.

The dialogs opened but did not close: React unmounts a node the instant
its state says so, so an exit animation never gets a frame to play. A
small presence hook holds each node for the length of its exit and marks
it inert while it leaves, so what is on screen for that tenth of a
second is a picture of a sheet rather than a sheet you can still tab
into. The exits are written as their own keyframes rather than as the
entrance played `reverse` — reversing an animation that has already
finished re-reads the same finished playhead against the other end of
the timeline, which snaps to the far keyframe instead of travelling to
it. The palette backdrop was also outliving the panel it dimmed for;
they now leave together.

The browser's own chrome — the address bar, the task switcher — was
keyed off the reader's OS rather than the theme they picked on the site,
because a media-conditioned `theme-color` pair cannot know about a
manual override. A client tag with no media wins by tree order, so it is
prepended rather than appended.

And the hero plate was a fixed height guessing at its own artwork's
shape. It now carries the ratio the drawing actually has, which measures
569x362.27 at 1440 — the same numbers as the reference.

Entire-Checkpoint: f245a63652e3","messageHeadline":"fix: let the overlays leave, and the browser chrome follow the reader","oid":"3deb19770613ca1099d7e35bf964fac41fa1d2b6"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T07:04:48Z","authors":[{"email":"dhruv2mars@gmail.com","id":"U_kgDOCn-7SQ","login":"Dhruv2mars","name":"Dhruv2mars"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-19T07:04:48Z","messageBody":"Two facts the usual social row cannot carry: a place and an hour.

They sit under the positioning line in the overview, each behind its own
glyph in the reference's icon-tile recipe, in mono, two to a row above
the small breakpoint. The location links to a map search on the same
string it displays, so there is nothing to keep in sync; it is unset for
now and an unset location draws no row rather than an empty pin.

The clock is real. One module-scope store ticks for the whole page and
only while something is subscribed, and the hands on the dial are drawn
from the actual time rather than frozen at ten past ten. The server
renders no time at all — this page is prerendered and revalidates
hourly, so a baked-in hour could be an hour wrong, and a clock that is
briefly blank beats a clock that is briefly wrong. Dashes hold the width
until the real time lands.

The distance to the reader keeps its minutes where the reference floors
to whole hours: from a half-hour zone that floor reports five where the
answer is five and a half, which is wrong rather than round.

pays a query-state dependency, a Suspense boundary and a router write
per keystroke for a shareable filtered index, and nobody shares one.

shape, the date formatter and the matcher move to lib/posts, which has
no filesystem in it; lib/blog keeps the disk. Bodies are dropped before
the list crosses to the browser.

closes every route, which is the standard practice it was measured
against.
